- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then decay too slowly — suggesting lag in recognizing downward momentum.
- After a spike in price (e.g., 72+), model often overreacts with a prolonged high forecast, failing to account for mean reversion.
- Model underestimates the rate of decline in later days, particularly when true values drop below 65.
- Forecasts show a persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is below 70.
- Model fails to adjust for recent downward trends — e.g., if last 5 days are falling, forecast still shows upward bias.
- Overshoots are more common in the first 10 days of forecast, then gradually correct — suggesting model doesn’t fully capture short-term volatility.
- When true values dip below 62, model often fails to recognize the drop and continues to forecast above 65.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent low values are not sufficiently weighted in forecasts, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjust — suggesting model doesn’t fully capture near-term volatility or policy shocks.
